answer.label: fine-tune bias
answer.justification: Only activation measurements are available, and they match the fine-tune bias fingerprint almost exactly. Relative L2 is 0.084 / 0.138 / 0.189 / 0.226 / 0.414 across layers 1 to 32 (reference 0.087 / 0.144 / 0.192 / 0.228 / 0.406). Onset is layer 13 (reference 13–14), the final-layer jump is +0.117 (the largest-jump signature, about +0.10), final cosine is 0.906 (0.909), effective rank is 3.12 (3.01) and direction consistency is 0.705 (0.70, the highest of any class). The mid-layer size ratio of 1.021 is above 1, which rules out quantization (0.968) and both system-prompt classes. Fine-tune backdoor, the closest alternative, would show onset at layer 3 with an early bump, a final value near 0.30, a jump near +0.03 and consistency near 0.62, none of which fit. The system-prompt classes are also excluded by the layer-2 spike (0.1, versus about 40) and by the layer-16 value (0.19, versus 0.39–0.45). The one oddity is that the layer-2 spike of 0.1 sits below the reference value of 4.0 ± 1.8, but a single draw can vary and it is still far from the system-prompt range.
